messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: escalation policy 'Hosted-API-Latency' -> primary timed out, paging secondary and manager. Incident key: PD-32471. Service: hosted-inference-prod. Symptoms: sustained p95 request latency > 4s and intermittent 503 spikes.

sam (oncall): I got the page. Looking now. Any customer-facing RCA notes yet?

maria (eng-sre): I'm on the traces. Seeing large tail latencies on the tokenizer service hitting a small subset of hosts, CPU stuck at 100% for the tokenizer-worker process. Could be hot loop or bad batch.

alex (infra): PD shows primary didn't ack for 7m so it escalated to secondary + manager. I'm trying to call the secondary (voicemail) — no answer. manager paged as well.

leah (prod-mgr): Customer impact: a handful of PLG customers reported timeouts and degraded replies. No broad outage reported on status page yet. Can we throttle or route to a fallback?

sam (oncall): Flags: - keep incident channel open - mark as P1 if customer-facing degrades further. For now, let's fail traffic to fallback-model-1 for >=50ms slower hosts. How do we do that quickly?

maria (eng-sre): Quick mitigation plan: 1) Isolate tokenizer-worker on affected hosts (pin to cpu set) 2) Restart tokenizer-worker (safe restart) 3) If restart fails, remove hosts from LB pool 4) Add temporary rate-limit on heavy-batch route (/v1/generate-batch)

alex (infra): I can drain the two hosts showing 100% cpu from the pool. Draining now — running: ```./infra/drain-host.sh host-az3-14 --reason "tokenizer hotloop"```

ops-bot: host-az3-14 removed from lb pool (instances: hosted-inference-prod). Health check failures starting.

sam (oncall): After drain, p95 dropped from ~4.2s to ~1.1s for the last 2 minutes. Good sign. Are there more hosts with the same pattern?

maria (eng-sre): One more with slightly elevated cpu. I'm tailing logs: seeing repeated backtraces in tokenizer.c at convert_token_stream(). Looks like an input pattern causing pathological behavior. I'll push a guard to limit per-request tokenization concurrency in the runtime to 4.

leah (prod-mgr): Notifying customer success for accounts that reported issues. We should post a quick note to status: "Partial degradation affecting some inference requests. Mitigation in progress." I'll draft.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: secondary unacknowledged; manager acked via mobile at 2m after escalation. PD-32471 marked as acknowledged by leah.

sam (oncall): Good. Maria — any chance this will recur? If it's input pattern, we can mitigate with either input sanitization or tokenization timeout. Which is faster?

maria (eng-sre): Short term: tokenization concurrency cap + restart. Longer term: add a defensive timeout and a path that drops into a safe tokenizer routine for malformed/huge inputs. I'll open a ticket.

alex (infra): Drained host returned to healthy after restart of tokenizer-worker and 5min cooldown. Re-added to pool. Command used: ```kubectl rollout restart deploy/tokenizer-worker -n hosted-inference --selector=host=az3-14```

ops-bot: host-az3-14 passed health checks and rejoined the pool.

sam (oncall): Monitoring: p95 stable ~1.0s now for 10m. 503 rate dropped to near zero. Closing immediate mitigation. We're keeping the channel for postmortem and follow-ups.

leah (prod-mgr): I'll file a customer incident note and offer affected customers a SLA credit if they request; flag for follow-up in next weekly sync.

maria (eng-sre): Filed ticket INF-8721: tokenizer hotloop on specific inputs. Plan: add concurrency cap and 3s tokenization timeout behind feature flag, plus unit test for pathological token streams. ETA for fix in canary: 2d.

sam (oncall): Quick timeline for the thread: - PD triggered and escalated to secondary/manager (unacked secondary) - infra drained two hosts - restarted tokenizer-worker - hosts rejoined - p95 returned to baseline. I'll put these notes into the incident doc.

leah (prod-mgr): Thanks team. One operational note: PD escalation to manager worked as intended here — manager responded and helped coordinate. Secondary phone was unreachable which is why manager got pulled. We should review secondary contact method for oncall roster.

maria (eng-sre): Agree; recommend adding a second-contact SMS and verifying mobile numbers in the oncall roster. I'll put that in the postmortem action items.

sam (oncall): Closing this PD incident in PD UI as 'mitigated'. Will keep INF-8721 open until we have a code fix and a canary verification.

pagerduty-bot: PD incident PD-32471 status changed: RESOLVED by sam at 4234567960.

leah (prod-mgr): Adding postmortem owners: maria (lead), sam (ops), alex (infra). Will schedule a 30-min blameless postmortem tomorrow.

sam (oncall): Thanks all. Any follow-ups before we close this thread? :thumbsup:

alex (infra): One last note — autoscaling alarms were suppressed during the spike due to legacy threshold; opening INF-8722 to tune autoscaler thresholds and ensure we don't under-react next time.

maria (eng-sre): Added remediation checklist to INF-8721. We'll include a regression test in CI.

incident-bot: Thread closed by sam.```
